podcast_name: What Keeps You Up at Night
episode_title: Get Up Now - Time is of the Essence
question: What are Kanae Corder's four choices when a challenge or obstacle comes into your way?
transcript_excerpt: When a challenge or an obstacle comes into your way you have four choices: you go over, you go under, you go around, or you sit your ass down. Sometimes you have to take what is called a presidential pause, but if you've been presidential pausing over and over again, it has to stop because if you keep pausing, you're never going to get where you're going.

podcast_name: What Keeps You Up at Night
episode_title: Get Up Now - Time is of the Essence
question: Why does Kanae Corder emphasize that familiar patterns keep people looping even when they are not working?
transcript_excerpt: The reason why you're not breaking the loop is because it's familiar and familiar feels good. Even when it feels bad, it feels better than the unknown. If familiar keeps you looping and looping isn't working, then you should try one of the other options: go over, go under, or go around.

podcast_name: What Keeps You Up at Night
episode_title: Get Up Now - Time is of the Essence
question: What does Kanae Corder teach about focus and expansion in personal transformation?
transcript_excerpt: What you focus on expands. So if you're focusing on what you don't want, you're going to get more of what you don't want. If you're focusing on what you don't do well, you're going to get more tasks that fall into that area where you don't do it well. Focus on what you want.

podcast_name: What Keeps You Up at Night
episode_title: Get Up Now - Time is of the Essence
question: What is Kanae Corder's advice for preparing financially as the recession and crash approach?
transcript_excerpt: Time is of the essence. The recession is happening right now. The crash is coming and when it comes, it's going to come fast and it's going to last long. You need to get your revenue up right now and you need to do it quickly. You should get up, get your revenue up, pay off debt, save some money, and lower your expenses wherever you can, but not so much that you feel deprived.

podcast_name: What Keeps You Up at Night
episode_title: Get Up Now - Time is of the Essence
question: How does Kanae Corder describe the relationship between trust, process, and receiving help from others?
transcript_excerpt: You've got to trust yourself, trust the process, and you need to trust the person you serve. In the moment, they may not know what you're saying, may not hear you, may not be able to ask you for what they need. It's not necessarily your job to figure it out, but you can get some help. Your ladder could be a friend, it could be a course, it could be a talk with someone—what is your ladder and what supplies do you need to move forward?
